gloss: here and there; all over the place

definitions.gloss: here and there; all over; in every direction
definitions.explanation: Refers to many scattered places at once, or to moving between them. Casual in tone; it works both as an adverb of place and as a noun taking particles.

examples.japanese: あっちこっち{探|さが}した。
examples.english: I looked all over the place.

examples.japanese: {部屋|へや}のあっちこっちに{本|ほん}が{置|お}いてある。
examples.english: There are books lying around all over the room.

examples.japanese: {道|みち}に{迷|まよ}って、あっちこっち{歩|ある}き{回|まわ}っているうちに{日|ひ}が{暮|く}れた。
examples.english: I got lost, and while I was wandering around here and there the sun went down.

notes:
A casual doubling of あっち (over there) and こっち (over here). Note the order: Japanese says "there and here," the reverse of the English idiom.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- あっちこっち{探|さが}す: to search everywhere
- あっちこっち{行|い}く: to go all over
- あっちこっちに: scattered in various places
- あっちこっちから: from all directions

REGISTER:
あっちこっち is conversational. The neutral equivalent is あちこち, and {方々|ほうぼう} is the formal written form; use one of those in writing or polite speech.
